questions.q: What is a typical meal in Bangladesh?
questions.answer: Rice is the foundation of almost every meal, usually with fish curry, lentils and some vegetables. There's even a saying that fish and rice make a Bengali, so it's [[deeply rooted]] in our identity.

questions.q: Is food an important part of your culture?
questions.answer: Enormously. In Bangladesh, food is at the centre of almost every gathering. Sharing a meal is how we express [[hospitality]], so it's really far more than just eating.

Hilsa cooked in mustard sauce, without question. Hilsa is our national fish, and my mother's version is [[unrivalled]] in my opinion. Coming from a river town, fresh fish is something I'd miss terribly if I lived abroad.

questions.q: Can you cook any local dishes?
questions.answer: Only a few basic ones, like dal and a simple egg curry. My mother is an excellent cook, so I've never really had to [[fend for myself]] in the kitchen, which I know will have to change if I study abroad.

questions.q: Has the food in your country changed in recent years?
questions.answer: Quite noticeably. Fast food outlets and cafés have [[mushroomed]] in towns as well as cities, and young people love burgers and pizza. Still, when it comes to family gatherings, traditional home cooking always wins.
